title: AGENTS.md — CanadaForestAllometry
text: CanadaForestAllometry provides unified interface published allometric models Canadian forests: tree volume (total merchantable), aboveground biomass (AGB), volume--biomass conversion, site index / productivity, supporting utilities. Models implemented faithfully source publications exposed consistent, vectorized API. Version: see DESCRIPTION (currently 0.8.7) License: LGPL (>= 3); Copyright Majesty King Right Canada (NRCan) R: >= 4.1.0 Imports: dplyr, tibble, tidyr, stringr, cli, rlang, purrr, stats, stringi, glue Docs site: https://ptompalski.github.io/CanadaForestAllometry/

title: AGENTS.md — CanadaForestAllometry
text: Function names encode model lineage prefix_[author][year]: Internal per-element helpers use leading dot / _one suffix (e.g. .thrower1994_height_one). Argument naming rule (package-wide): acronyms upper case, words lower case — DBH (cm), BA (m²/ha), TPH (stems/ha), HDOM (m), HTOP (m, top height), QMD (cm), DMEAN (cm), DDOM (cm), DMAX (cm, plot maximum DBH), BAL (m²/ha), climate MAT (°C), MAP (mm), GDD; height, age, species, jurisdiction, elevation. Exception: site index si (m). Tree- vs plot-level stated @param, encoded case. use source-language symbols (e.g. TMOY, SDOM) argument names; map inside function note source symbol @param. Region / ecological arguments use model-specific descriptive names (natural_subregion, ecozone, ecoregion, bec_zone, district, bioclim_subdomain, …), never generic subregion. vol() (dispatcher) get_volume_params() (table filter) take subregion. registry subregion_arg / region_arg must name engine’s actual argument. Model-variant selectors called variant (character, rlang::arg_match). Flags keep_* (extra output columns, e.g. keep_model_id) include_*, scalar logicals. Argument order: DBH/age, height/si, species, region, predictors, options/flags.

title: AGENTS.md — CanadaForestAllometry
text: Vectorized: user-facing model functions operate element-wise safe inside dplyr::mutate(). Inputs recycled common length; incompatible lengths raise explicit error. rowwise()/pmap() wrappers required. Return tibbles snake_case columns (e.g. vol_total, vol_merchantable). Stable public API — preserve signatures return types unless change explicitly requested. Species codes: NFI format GENUS.SPEC (e.g. PICE.MAR = black spruce); compact PICEGLA accepted normalized; genus-level PICE.SPP supported. Use translate_species_code() convert NFI, CANFI, jurisdiction, common/scientific names. Jurisdiction / subregion: 2-letter province codes (AB, BC, , QC, …); parameter lookups apply subregion fallback logic models require . Validation: user-facing functions validate early cli/rlang-style structured errors; internal helpers may assume validated inputs.

title: Tree Volume Models
text: several individual tree volume allometric models designed Canadian forests. developed jurisdiction level require DBH, height, species inputs. package currently includes: vol_fortin2007(). Provincial merchantable volume model Quebec. Coverage: QC. 26 species vol_galbella94(). Provincial taper model Saskatchewan based Kozak variable-exponent form. Coverage: SK. 12 species vol_honer83(). Regional volume models central eastern Canada, applicable across multiple provinces. Coverage: NB, NL, NS, , PE, QC. 21 species vol_huang94(). Provincial taper model Alberta based Kozak variable-exponent form; applicable province level Alberta subregions. Coverage: AB. 13 species vol_klos2007(). Provincial taper model Manitoba based Kozak variable-exponent form; applicable province level ecozone. Coverage: MB. 5 species vol_kozak94(). Provincial taper model British Columbia; requires BEC zone subregion input. Coverage: BC. 16 species vol_nigh2016(). Total merchantable volume equations BC. Coverage: BC. 18 species vol_nl(). Coverage: NB, NL, NS, , PE, QC. 25 species vol_ung2013(). National taper model Canada, available two variants: DBH-DBH total height. Coverage: Canada (national). 34 species vol_zakrzewski2013(). what: vol(): automatic tree volume estimation across multiple models
title: Tree Volume Models
text: vol() convenience wrapper estimating total merchantable tree volume using volume models implemented CanadaForestAllometry. Rather requiring users select specific model, vol() uses internal model registry automatically determines models applicable tree based : species availability model parameter tables geographic scope (province/jurisdiction) required inputs (e.g. total height, subregion BEC zone) model ranking (regional models preferred national available) Example:
code: trees <- tibble::tibble(   DBH = c(18, 22, 30, 26, 20),   height = c(15, 18, 22, 20, 20),   species = c("PICE.MAR", "BETU.PAP", "POPU.TRE", "PSEU.MEN", "PINU.BAN"),   jurisdiction =  c("AB", "ON", "QC", "BC", "MB"),   subregion = c(NA, NA, NA, "CWH", "Boreal Plains") )  trees |>   dplyr::mutate(     vol(       DBH = DBH,       height = height,       species = species,       jurisdiction = jurisdiction,       subregion = subregion,       keep_model_id = TRUE     )   ) #> # A tibble: 5 × 8 #>     DBH height species  jurisdiction subregion     vol_total vol_merchantable #>   <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>    <chr>        <chr>             <dbl>            <dbl> #> 1    18     15 PICE.MAR AB           <NA>              0.158            0.145 #> 2    22     18 BETU.PAP ON           <NA>              0.291            0.233 #> 3    30     22 POPU.TRE QC           <NA>             NA                0.674 #> 4    26     20 PSEU.MEN BC           CWH               0.387            0.305 #> 5    20     20 PINU.BAN MB           Boreal Plains     0.291            0.274 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: model_id <chr>

title: Tree Volume Models
text: Merchantable volume CanadaForestAllometry defined using jurisdiction-specific merchantability rules, following officially adopted criteria province territory (e.g., minimum top diameter, minimum DBH, stump height). models, rules applied dynamically based provided jurisdiction. volume models, however, merchantability criteria fixed within model formulation , reflecting original equations developed calibrated. cases (e.g., vol_honer83(), vol_sharma2021(), vol_fortin2007(), vol_nigh2016()), merchantable volume computed using model-specific, hard-coded criteria vary jurisdiction species. jurisdiction-specific merchantability criteria used CanadaForestAllometry can inspected built-dataset merchcrit, documents values applied jurisdiction (, applicable, species subregion).

title: Tree Volume Models
text: Tree stem volume estimated Canada using variety model families, ranging national equations (e.g., Ung et al. (2013)) province-specific taper volume systems (e.g., Kozak (1994), Huang et al. (1994), Zakrzewski Penner (2013), Sharma (2021)). models differ functional form, calibration data, jurisdictional scope. CanadaForestAllometry package implements models unified interface, allowing consistent input formatting transparent model selection. However, different equations may yield systematically different predictions tree dimensions. figure shows total merchantable volume calculated using implemented models (x-axis) across species. provides quick overview species coverage (.e., species covered model) highlights differences among model outputs, tree DBH height held constant every calculation.

title: Allometric models for Canadian forest
text: CanadaForestAllometry R package brings together collection published allometric models developed Canadian forests. package provides unified interface estimate range tree- stand-level attributes, based models published Canadian forestry literature. focus CanadaForestAllometry standardization: models implemented faithfully possible original formulations, transparent parameter tables, consistent inputs/outputs, jurisdiction-appropriate assumptions (e.g. merchantability rules). Part package standardization use NFI species codes implemented models (e.g. PICE.MAR black spruce). package also includes translate_species_code(), can translate among jurisdiction-specific codes, NFI CANFI codes, common English French names, scientific names.

what: Ung2009 Growth and Yield Model — Ung2009
title: Ung2009 Growth and Yield Model — Ung2009
text: function implements models described Ung et al. (2009). Two models (Nat1 Nat2) available: Nat1: multi-equation system predicting tree height (H), basal area (BA), volume (V) based stand age, growth degree days (GDD), annual precipitation (MAP), species-specific parameters. Nat2: single equation focuses predicting stand volume (V) using age, GDD, MAP.

title: Ung2009 Growth and Yield Model — Ung2009
code: Ung2009(age, species, GDD, MAP, variant = c("both", "Nat1", "Nat2"))

title: Ung2009 Growth and Yield Model — Ung2009
text: age Numeric vector. age(s) stand years. Must greater 0. species Character. valid species name defined parameter table model. GDD Numeric. Growth degree days. MAP Numeric. Annual precipitation (source "PREC"). variant Character. model(s) use. One "Nat1", "Nat2", "". Defaults "".

title: Ung2009 Growth and Yield Model — Ung2009
text: tibble containing: age H (Nat1 used): Predicted tree height (m). BA (Nat1 used): Predicted basal area (m²/ha). V (Nat1 used): Predicted volume (m³/ha). V2 (Nat2 used): Predicted volume (m³/ha) based Nat2 model.

title: Ung2009 Growth and Yield Model — Ung2009
text: Nat1 model, height basal area modeled using age, GDD, MAP Chapman-Richards formulation, volume derived via allometric equation. contrast, Nat2 streamlined, modeling volume directly function variables without explicit height basal area components.

title: Ung2009 Growth and Yield Model — Ung2009

Stand origin: plantation-models used stand_origin = "plantation". plantation trees, models fitted plantations (origins) preferred; natural-stand models used fallback, warning. British Columbia coast vs interior: models fitted coastal interior BC (see bc_region hd_model_registry()) restricted trees region bec_zone bc_region given. neither given, remain eligible warning issued one used. Required predictors: every required predictor model (see get_hd_model_info()) must supplied ... non-missing tree. Optional predictors (e.g. region code) passed non-missing. Ranking: among eligible models highest rank used. model fails tree (e.g. species-specific predictor missing, region code recognised), next-ranked model tried.

title: Auger (2016) DBH–height model for 27 Québec tree species — hd_auger2016
text: Model form (equation 1, p. 4): $$h = 1.3 + \ln(DBH + 1) + B \ln(DBH + 1)^2,$$ $$= + a_{ST} BA + a_{RDHP} \frac{DBH}{QMD} + a_{ALT} ALT +   a_{PTOT} PTOT + a_{TMOY} TMOY + a_{SDOM} + a_{MP} + a_{VP} + a_{PERT},$$ \(B\) species constant every covariate effect interacts \(\ln(DBH + 1)\). Source symbols map arguments : ALT = elevation, PTOT = MAP, TMOY = MAT, SDOM = bioclim_subdomain, MP = physical_env, VP = potential_veg, PERT = disturbance. Height transformed, back-transformation applies. Grey birch (BETU.POP) \(\ln(DBH + 1)^2\) term source (Annexe 1) linear \(\ln(DBH + 1)\). Species-specific predictors (Tableau 5, pp. 10–11): BA used species; predictors species whose selected model contains . predictor required row's species uses ; otherwise may NULL NA ignored. Use get_hd_model_info("auger2016") definitions, see source per-species predictor sets. example, white spruce (PICE.GLA) uses BA, QMD, MAT, bioclim_subdomain potential_veg; silver maple, American elm grey birch use BA . Population-level prediction: published fixed effects plot random effect residual set zero, .e. marginal prediction used source (p. 7). Plot calibration measured heights implemented. Class codes: classes observations grouped author, group estimate repeated member class (Annexes 2–4). class estimate species (absent fitting data, e.g. physical environment 7 red oak) gives NA height one warning per call. Codes matched case-insensitively. Coefficient precision: coefficients used printed (4 decimals). altitude precipitation slopes therefore carry one significant digit; rounding can shift predictions 0.15 m. Applicability: fitted merchantable trees (DBH \(\ge\) 9.1 cm) Québec permanent temporary inventory plots. author advises use trees DBH < 9 cm (p. 19); trees computed reported outside range, predicted height may 1.3 m. Inputs outside per-species ranges fitting data (Tableau 1: DBH relative DBH; Tableau 2: BA, elevation, MAT, MAP) computed reported single warning. Rows NA used input return NA height. External implementation: generalhdrelation2014 module CFSForestTools reproduces published coefficients 10 species (PRUN.SER, ACER.SAC, FRAX.AME, FRAX.NIG, LARI.LAR, ULMU.AME, OSTR.VIR, PINU.STR, PINU.RES, TILI.AME; within 0.02 m) uses different parameter estimates predictor sets 17 species (differences 2.6 m). function follows publication.

title: Auger, DeBlois & Lambert (2025) DBH–height models for Québec plantations — hd_auger2025
text: Model scope: black spruce (PICE.MAR, source "EPN") jack pine (PINU.BAN, source "PIG") monospecific plantations Québec plantation monitoring network (p. 2). models fitted natural stands; stand origin checked function. Variants (chosen variant): "dbh" (default) Korf form, eq. 10 (Tableau 7, p. 11), species: $$H = 1.3 + \alpha_1 \exp(-\alpha_2 DBH^{-\alpha_3}).$$ Estimates mean height population given DBH; authors note shape unlikely suit particular plot (pp. 4–5). "plot_mean_dbh" Requires DMEAN. Jack pine, eq. 11 (Chapman–Richards) black spruce, eq. 12 (Hossfeld II) (Tableau 8, p. 14): $$PIG: H = 1.3 + (\alpha_{10} + \alpha_{11} MD)       [1 - \exp(-(\alpha_{20} + \alpha_{21} MD) DBH)]^{\alpha_3};$$ $$EPN: H = 1.3 + (\alpha_{10} + \alpha_{11} MD)       \frac{DBH^{\alpha_3}}{(\alpha_{20} + \alpha_{21} MD) + DBH^{\alpha_3}},$$ \(MD\) DMEAN. "dominant" Requires HDOM DDOM. Jack pine, eq. 13 black spruce, eq. 14 (Tableau 9, p. 17), forms \(\alpha_{10} + \alpha_{11} HDOM\) asymptote term \(\alpha_{20} + \alpha_{22} DD\) rate/scale term, \(DD\) DDOM. Predictors used selected variant ignored warning. Height convention: total tree height; DBH measured 1.3 m every form tends 1.3 m DBH tends 0. Fit: weighted fixed-effects nonlinear regressions; plot random effect improve fit none included (pp. 5–7), published coefficients used directly. Variance-function parameters used. Korf asymptote: published \(\alpha_1\) values large (1,630,094 m jack pine 101,489 m black spruce), "dbh" curves keep increasing beyond data. Extrapolation beyond calibration DBH range recommended. Rows NA used input return NA height. Inputs outside per-species calibration ranges (Tableau 1, p. 4: DBH , depending variant, mean DBH, dominant height dominant DBH) computed reported single warning. worked example table predicted heights published; implementation checked plausibility (see data-raw/Auger2025_model-spec.md).

text: Model scope (species coverage): eastern white pine (PINU.STR), eastern white cedar (THUJ.OCC), sugar maple (ACER.SAH), yellow birch (BETU.), American beech (FAGU.GRA), tamarack (LARI.LAR), basswood (TILI.AME) eastern hemlock (TSUG.CAN). Fitted Ontario growth--yield NFI plots natural stands (Table 1, p. 219), stand basal area \(\ge\) 5 m²/ha. Model forms (eqs. 4 5, p. 220): $$M4: H = 1.3 + \alpha_0 [1 - \exp(-\alpha_1 DBH)]^{\alpha_2};$$ $$M5: H = 1.3 + \alpha_0 \, HDOM^{\alpha_1}   [1 - \exp(-\alpha_2 (TPH / BA)^{\alpha_3} DBH)]^{\alpha_4}.$$ Height convention: total tree height; DBH measured 1.3 m, predicted height tends 1.3 m DBH tends 0. Population-level prediction: coefficients fixed effects mixed-effects fits (Tables 4 5, p. 225), evaluated plot-level random effect \(\alpha_0\) set zero (\(u = 0\)), "fixed response" curves Fig. 3. Plot-specific calibration measured heights implemented. Variants: HDOM, BA TPH NULL (default), M4 (DBH ) used. three supplied, M5 used every species. Supplying error. one-time message reports variant used. authors note M4 performed well better M5 yellow birch eastern hemlock (basswood) M4 "may considered parsimonious operationally practical model cases stand-level variables unavailable unreliable" (p. 222, p. 225). Tamarack basswood (M5): stand-density exponent \(\alpha_3\) reported 0 (significant; Table 5), BA TPH change predicted heights; still required M5. Corrected coefficient: tamarack M5 \(\alpha_2\) printed 0.9793 Table 5, gives near-flat curve (16 m DBH 2.5 cm) inconsistent Fig. 3b fitting data (Table 1). treated misprint 0.09793 used, reproduces tamarack curve Fig. 3b. value inferred, published. authors report increased bias DBH > 50 cm, particularly white pine, sugar maple, beech hemlock (p. 225). Rows NA input return NA height. Inputs outside per-species range fitting data (Table 1: DBH , M5, HDOM, BA TPH) computed reported single warning.

text: Model scope: black spruce . Fitted 93 Alberta permanent sample plots (917 trees) Lower Foothills natural region validated 71 plots Boreal Mixedwood Upper Foothills (p. 4). Model forms (eqs. 9–11, pp. 4–5): $$(9): H = 1.3 + \beta_1 [1 - \exp(-\beta_2 DBH)]^{\beta_3};$$ $$(10): H = 1.3 + (\beta_1 + \beta_4 HTOP) [1 - \exp(-\beta_2 DBH)]^{\beta_3};$$ $$(11): H = 1.3 + (\beta_1 + \beta_4 HTOP + \beta_5 BA)   [1 - \exp(-\beta_2 DBH)]^{\beta_3}.$$ Height convention: total tree height; DBH measured 1.3 m, predicted height tends 1.3 m DBH tends 0. Population-level prediction: coefficients fixed effects nonlinear mixed models (Table 2, p. 13), evaluated plot random effects \(\beta_1\) \(\beta_3\) set zero (source's "fixed " predictions, Table 3). Plot-specific calibration measured heights implemented. authors report fixed-predictions biased individual plots average (Table 4: mean bias −7.5%, −2.1% −3.3% mean height validation data models 9, 10 11), base model (9) gave accurate calibrated predictions despite ranking last AIC/BIC. ratio correction describe (eqs. 29–30) published value applied. Variants: HTOP BA NULL (default), model 9 used; HTOP supplied, model 10; supplied, model 11. Supplying BA without HTOP error. one-time message reports variant used. Rows NA input return NA height. Inputs outside range fitting data (Table 1: DBH , used, HTOP BA) computed reported single warning.

title: Rijal, Weiskittel and Kershaw (2012) DBH–height models for the Acadian Region — hd_rijal2012
text: Model scope (species coverage): American beech (FAGU.GRA), grey birch (BETU.POP), paper birch (BETU.PAP), trembling aspen (POPU.TRE), red maple (ACER.RUB), northern red oak (QUER.RUB), sugar maple (ACER.SAH), yellow birch (BETU.), balsam fir (ABIE.BAL), black spruce (PICE.MAR), eastern hemlock (TSUG.CAN), red spruce (PICE.RUB), eastern white cedar (THUJ.OCC), eastern white pine (PINU.STR) white spruce (PICE.GLA). Fitted permanent research plots, mostly mixed-species, uneven-aged stands (pp. 380–381). Model form (eq. 4, p. 381): $$HT = 1.37 + (c_0 + CSI^{c_3})   [1 - \exp(-c_1 DBH)]^{c_2 + c_4 \ln(CCF + 1) + c_5 BAL}.$$ Variants (chosen variant): "gnls" (default) uses generalized nonlinear least-squares coefficients (Table 5, p. 387), authors recommend "observations available local calibration" (p. 386). "nlme" uses fixed effects nonlinear mixed-effects fit (Table 6, p. 387) source, stand year random effects \(c_0\) set zero; without local calibration biased GNLS (p. 386). grey birch northern red oak NLME BAL coefficient significant (printed "–") zero. Height convention: total tree height. 1.37 m intercept (US breast height) used data, although Canadian DBH measured 1.3 m; authors judged difference negligible (p. 381). Predicted height 1.37 m DBH 0. Rows NA input return NA height. DBH outside per-species range fitting data (Table 1, p. 381) computed reported single warning. source gives ranges CSI, CCF BAL; inputs extreme enough make exponent non-positive raise error.

title: Sharma (2016) DBH–height models for Ontario plantations and natural stands — hd_sharma2016
text: Model scope (species coverage): jack pine (PINU.BAN), red pine (PINU.RES), black spruce (PICE.MAR) white spruce (PICE.GLA), plantation natural-stand parameter set. Fitted Ontario permanent sample plots (400 m²); red pine plots mostly southwest province, species cover boreal region (p. 71). Model form (eq. 4, p. 75; form Sharma Parton 2007, see hd_sharmaparton2007()): $$H = 1.3 + \theta \, HDOM^{\delta}   [1 - \exp(-\beta (TPH / BA)^{\phi} DBH)]^{\gamma}.$$ Height convention: total tree height; DBH measured 1.3 m, predicted height tends 1.3 m DBH tends 0. Population-level prediction: coefficients fixed effects mixed-effects fit (Table 3, p. 74), evaluated plot-level random effect \(\theta\) set zero (\(u = 0\)), Fig. 4 source. Plot-specific calibration measured heights implemented. Notes published coefficients: published, \(\phi\) negative red pine natural stands, \(\delta\) \(\phi\) negative black spruce natural stands (p. 75). , predicted height decreases slightly TPH / BA (, natural black spruce, HDOM). \(\phi\) white spruce plantations blank Table 3 (non-significant parameter, p. 75). set 0 , TPH / BA term drops BA TPH affect model. Table 3 exactly reproduce curves Fig. 4 large DBH (differences 1.2 m 40 cm); function implements Table 3 published. Rows NA input return NA height. Inputs outside range fitting data species stand origin (DBH, Table 2; BA, TPH HDOM, Table 1; p. 72) computed reported single warning.

title: Staudhammer and LeMay (2000) DBH–height models for coastal British Columbia — hd_staudhammerlemay2000
text: Model scope: fitted 1995 inventory UBC Malcolm Knapp Research Forest (5000 ha, Coastal Western Hemlock zone, coastal BC): 327 plots 82 clusters, heights measured subjectively chosen subset 763 trees (p. 304). source alder model ("D") combines Alnus rubra . tenuifolia; used red alder (ALNU.RUB) . Alder 28 trees 16 plots. Model form (eq. 2, Yang et al. 1978; p. 305): $$H = 1.3 + E_1 [1 - \exp(E_2 \, DBH^{E_3})].$$ intercept constrained 1.3 m DBH = 0. Variants (chosen variant): "dbh" (default): eq. 2, \(E_1\), \(E_2\), \(E_3\) species constants (Table 5, p. 308). four species. "density": parameter prediction (Table 5, p. 308). red alder (eq. 2a), \(E_k = c_{k0} + c_{k1} TPH + c_{k2} BA\). western redcedar, Douglas-fir western hemlock (eq. 2b), \(E_k = c_{k0} + c_{k1} R + c_{k2} R^2\), \(R = DBH / DMAX\) tree's relative DBH. TPH BA required data include red alder, DMAX include species. Within plot (fixed DMAX), eq. 2b heights increase DBH relative DBH 0.85–0.95 decrease slightly plot's largest trees; follows published quadratic \(R\). Predictors used selected variant species ignored warning. Coefficients ordinary nonlinear least-squares fits (SAS PROC NLIN); calibration information published. Corrected coefficient: western redcedar (eq. 2b), slope \(E_2\) \(R^2\) printed 0.1551. value \(E_2\) becomes positive \(R > 0.23\), giving negative heights (e.g. -47 m DBH = 30 cm, \(R\) = 0.5), inconsistent reported fit (RMSE 4.308 m, Table 2). value 0.01551 (dropped zero) used: gives plausible heights matches DBH-\(E_2\) \(R = 1\). correction inference, published erratum. Validity: far outside fitting data "density" parameters can become invalid (\(E_1 \le 0\), \(E_2 \ge 0\) \(E_3 \le 0\)): Douglas-fir \(R < 0.062\), redcedar \(R < 0.019\), hemlock \(R < 0.008\), red alder TPH 7900 stems/ha large BA low TPH. rows raise error; use variant = "dbh" . Inputs outside per-species ranges fitting data (Table 1, p. 304: DBH, "density" also TPH, BA \(R\)) computed reported single warning. Rows NA used input return NA height. source worked example, implementation checked plausibility .

Age definition note: age breast-height age (BHA, years). curve conditioned height = si BHA 50. Base-age note: site index site height breast-height age 50. Translate from scientific, English, or French names translate_species_code("Picea mariana", from = "scientificname") #> [1] "PICE.MAR" translate_species_code("black spruce", from = "englishname") #> [1] "PICE.MAR" translate_species_code("epinette noire", from = "frenchname") #> [1] "PICE.MAR"  # Translate from jurisdiction, CANFI, or auto-detected inputs translate_species_code("BF", from = "jurisdiction", jurisdiction = "ON") #> [1] "ABIE.BAL" translate_species_code("302", from = "canfi") #> [1] "ABIE.BAL" translate_species_code("302", from = "auto") #> Auto-detected input type: canfi #> [1] "ABIE.BAL"  # Translate between name fields translate_species_code("black spruce", from = "englishname", to = "frenchname") #> [1] "épinette noire" translate_species_code("Picea mariana", from = "scientificname", to = "englishname") #> [1] "black spruce" translate_species_code("PICE.GLA", from = "auto", to = "scientificname") #> Auto-detected input type: nfi #> [1] "Picea glauca"  # Auto-detect a shared jurisdiction from a vector of input codes translate_species_code(c("BF", "PJ", "SB"), from = "auto") #> Auto-detected input type: jurisdiction (on) #> [1] "ABIE.BAL" "PINU.BAN" "PICE.MAR" translate_species_code(   "SW",   from = "jurisdiction",   jurisdiction = "BC",   to = "scientificname" ) #> [1] "Picea glauca"  # text: Function arguments now follow one package-wide naming scheme (see AGENTS.md). old names removed, deprecation shims. Ung2009(): PREC -> MAP. Argument order now (age, species, GDD, MAP, variant). vol_total_to_merchantable(): include_prop -> include_props. si_nigh2004(): argument order now (age, height, si, species, bec_zone), matching si_*() functions. vol(): vol_model output column renamed model_id now holds registry model ID (e.g. "regional_huang94") instead engine name.
